_note: RULES569 R1 (S569, owner: 'what if we may a guard 1 action like both hands up and hands do not punch at the same time and move some things into the rules instead of having them as actions'): the four guard switches are gone. A hand that is not punching is back in its STANCE guard by itself - the lead glove in front of the chin (stops his jab and cross), the rear glove by the cheek (stops his lead hook and overhand); the body and the uppercut line are what a stance leaves open. GUARD UP is one card (in the lead-hand lane; it takes both hands for its moment, costs 1 stamina and the lead hand does not rest): every line is covered from its moment until his next action - alone in a beat, the whole beat. A feint still draws it. A punch blocked by the stance wears the guard bar (1, or 2 for a punch of 3 or more); a punch blocked by Guard up wears nothing. The two hands never punch in the same moment (already so: one action a moment). This is variant a2, the best of ten screened at n=12 (docs/RULES569_RESULT.md has the ten).
